industry: Residential handyman / odd-job repair, punch-list fixes, and light maintenance (drywall, fixtures, doors, minor plumbing/electrical where licensed to do so)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Licensed contractor' / 'fully licensed' if operating under a handyperson exemption or lacking the required license class
'Insured/bonded' if policies are lapsed or nonexistent
'We do electrical/plumbing' in jurisdictions requiring specialty licenses the sender lacks
'From $X/hour' that is rarely available; unclear trip fees
Fake urgency ('call in the next 10 minutes')
Unwarranted 'seniors only' targeting without a real discount program
compliance_notes: State contractor law varies. California example: B&P 7048 minor-work exemption — as amended, under $1,000 total, casual/minor, no building permit, not part of a larger project, and the person may not employ others; advertising as a contractor or implying contractor qualification removes the exemption. Unlicensed advertisers must disclose they are not licensed when advertising under the exemption (CSLB AB 2622 guidance).
Never advertise permit-required work or licensed trades without the proper license.
FTC s.5 / 16 CFR 233/251: free estimates, $ off, % off need clear conditions and bona fide prices.
'Insured/bonded' — only if true; consider stating what insurance covers at a high level if making strong safety claims.
Price 'from' / hourly: disclose trip fees and minimums that materially change the price.
39 USC 3001: no fake city inspection notices.
If using senior/veteran discounts, they must be real and non-deceptive; do not invent a senior audience default.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: relief, pride, anxiety-reduction, belonging are fine when legal.
Every angle and emotion_by_offer combo carries sell_the_outcome_line.
Vendor ROI labeled agency-only unverified; never print as fact on a client card.
Prefer one clear offer + one real photo + one QR (roofing-round5 directional).
No age/senior default unless real discount + evidence.
